title: Economy looks strong despite recession fears: Jobs, inflation & Trump tariffs explained
summary: Local news finance segment: January inflation came in cooler, jobs beat expectations, the economy is resilient with no recession in sight, but job gains are concentrated in health care.

assertions.quote: It's proving to be surprisingly resilient.

verdicts.note: Growth and payrolls held up in late 2025 and early 2026 with unemployment near 4.3%.

Real GDP grew 2.5% annualized in Q1 2026 and 2.2% in Q2, with consumer spending, investment and exports contributing, and unemployment stayed at 4.3-4.4% in early 2026; no contraction appears in the data for the period.

assertions.quote: almost all the jobs created, uh, in this last report were in the health care sector

verdicts.note: BLS payrolls in 2025-26 showed health care and social assistance accounting for most net gains.

Over the 12 months to September 2026 health care added an average 33,000 jobs a month against 45,000 for total nonfarm payrolls, about three quarters of all gains, with employment in all other major industries little changed; the release measures the concentration, and the 'weakness' reading is the claim's interpretation of that narrow base.

assertions.quote: Interest rates are stable and hopefully coming down.

verdicts.note: The Fed held in January 2026 and then raised rates in September 2026 as inflation climbed.

On September 16, 2026 the FOMC raised the federal funds target range by a quarter point to 3.75-4%, the opposite of the predicted fall; the statement does not show the early-2026 rate path, so this only settles the prediction's outcome.

assertions.quote: he is what is known as an interest rate hawk, meaning he aggressively wants to bring interest rates down

verdicts.note: A hawk favours higher rates to fight inflation; Warsh went on to raise rates in September 2026.
